findings.title: Retry-based deletion is not scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
findings.body: The new `deleteMany` clause `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` is combined with the original SMS/scheduledDate condition via `OR`, so it applies to any WorkflowReminder row of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) and any state (including already-scheduled ones) whose retryCount exceeds 1. The branch should be constrained the same way the rest of this cron job is: `method: SMS` and `scheduled: false`. Today only this SMS cron increments retryCount, so the damage is latent, but the moment any other code path (e.g. an email reminder retry) writes retryCount, this endpoint will silently delete those reminders, dropping emails/WhatsApp messages that were still pending.

findings.title: Retry counter uses stale read-then-write increments
findings.body: Both retry paths write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, where `reminder.retryCount` was read at query time. If two cron invocations overlap (slow Twilio calls make this plausible), both runs read the same value and both write the same incremented value, losing one failure count. Using a relative increment (`retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in Prisma) would make the counter accurate under concurrency and keep the retry limit behavior (delete after 2 failures) from being extended indefinitely.

findings.title: Reminders with missing sendTo never retry and are never counted
findings.body: The retry counter is only incremented inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` or in the catch block. When `sendTo` is empty (e.g. booking has no `smsReminderNumber`) or the message body resolves empty, the reminder is silently skipped with no increment, so it stays in the unscheduled set and is re-fetched and re-skipped on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. This is the exact 'invalid phone number' scenario the PR description targets, and it still results in an unbounded retry loop for that class of reminders; the skip branch should either increment retryCount or otherwise mark the reminder.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces a stateful behavior change (reminders are permanently deleted after two failed scheduling attempts, plus a new column and migration) but ships no unit or integration tests. There are no tests verifying that a reminder failing twice is deleted, that a reminder failing once is retried and can still succeed, or that successfully scheduled reminders are not affected by the retryCount cleanup. Given this code path silently deletes user-facing reminder data, regression coverage is warranted before merging.
